title: Using max on real lists
idea: TOOL applied: read best-so-far code for everyday 'which is largest' questions and predict results.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

temps = [18, 24, 19, 31, 22]
hottest = temps[0]
for t in temps:
    if t > hottest:
        hottest = t
print(hottest)
exercises.explanation: The warmest day is 31. The best-so-far climbs to 31 and nothing beats it.

exercises.prompt: Which variable name reads most clearly for the biggest score?
exercises.explanation: A descriptive name like top_score makes the code read like the problem. Bare names like x hide what it means.
Start longest at jumps[0], the first real value, then compare the rest. It will land on 7.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

sales = [120, 95, 120, 80]
best = sales[0]
for s in sales:
    if s > best:
        best = s
print(best)
exercises.explanation: The best day sold 120 (it appears twice). The loop reports 120 as the single biggest.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a program that prints the highest rating in a list called ratings.
exercises.explanation: Start best at the first rating, loop each rating, replace when bigger, then print the winner.

exercises.prompt: The best-so-far pattern works the same whether the list holds test scores, temperatures, or prices.
exercises.explanation: Max does not care what the numbers mean. The same loop finds the biggest of any list of numbers.

exercises.prompt: A shop tracks daily visitors: [40, 55, 55, 33]. The max loop reports 55. What does that 55 mean?
options: The busiest single day had 55 visitors
exercises.explanation: Max gives the single biggest value — here, the most visitors on any one day.

exercises.prompt: You need the WINNER'S score from [71, 88, 65]. Which pattern fits?
exercises.explanation: 'The winner's score' is the single highest value — a max problem.

exercises.prompt: Which problems call for the max pattern? (pick all)
options: The most goals in one game
exercises.explanation: Record high and most-in-one-game both want the single biggest value. Average and total are different tools.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [50]
best = n[0]
for x in n:
    if x > best:
        best = x
print(best)
exercises.explanation: With one value, best starts at 50 and the loop finds nothing bigger. The max of a one-item list is that item.
